questions.question: Explain what happens when a business is incorporated as a company, and how this gives its owners limited liability and continuity.
questions.expected_answer: Incorporation is registration with CIPC under the Companies Act 2008 (filing the MOI and notice of incorporation). It creates a separate legal person that owns assets, makes contracts, borrows and sues in its own name. Because the company owes its own debts, shareholders can lose only what they paid for their shares — limited liability (subject to exceptions such as personal guarantees and reckless trading). Because the company is a separate person, it continues when shareholders sell shares, retire or die — continuity.

questions.question: Compare a private company and a public company under: name ending, minimum directors, offering shares to the public, transfer of shares and publication/audit of financial statements.
questions.expected_answer: Private: (Pty) Ltd; at least one director; may not offer shares to the public; transfer restricted by MOI; statements not published, audit/independent review depends on public interest score. Public: Ltd; at least three directors (plus audit committee and company secretary); may offer shares to the public via a prospectus and may list on the JSE; shares freely transferable; annual statements must be audited and made available (published if listed); must hold an AGM.

questions.question: A company has 1 000 shares and declares a total dividend of R100 000. Calculate the dividend per share and the dividend received by a shareholder with 300 shares. An investor buys 100 shares at R50: what is her maximum loss, and her gain if the price rises to R80?
questions.expected_answer: Dividend per share = 100 000 ÷ 1 000 = R100. Shareholder with 300 shares: 300 × 100 = R30 000. Investment = 100 × 50 = R5 000 = maximum loss (limited liability). At R80: value = 100 × 80 = R8 000; gain = 8 000 − 5 000 = R3 000.
